reaction: It’s satisfying to see the separate nerve fibres gather into one bundle.

reaction: The separate jobs of the eye parts are clearer now.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it should bring the focusing front together with the light-sensitive lining.
expectation: I expect an eye with light focused toward the retina and an optic nerve ready to connect to the body.

reaction: The cutaway makes the arrangement of the parts easy to follow.
reason: This is the only available combination, and connecting the eye to the body advances the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the eye and its optic nerve to connect to the body and brain, though I’m unsure whether that alone will produce sight.

effect: The eyes and their nerves are connected to the body and brain, completing the chapter. The result does not show whether the leaf is actually seen.
reaction: The connection completes the model, though I expected to see more of how the leaf becomes a sight.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the retina and optic nerve was most worthwhile: it showed how the light-sensitive lining connects to an outgoing nerve.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the finished front to the retina felt predictable; it was the only combination offered and mostly assembled parts already explained.

surprise.text: I expected a demonstration of seeing the leaf, but completion showed the eyes connected to the brain without showing the leaf as a sight.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless. Adding the iris was the only available action, but its role in controlling light was clear.

continue.text: I might continue to see how signals become sight, but the mostly predictable assembly and lack of a leaf demonstration make the hook modest.
